Mobilization · Phase 5 Pattern Setter

The canonical 30/60/90 delivery plan + RACI + dependency graph that turns an approved strategy and business case into actual execution. Applies to every Move. Worked example: Move 0 — Kyriba De-Risk at Morgan Street. Owner: Aisha Vargas (Group Treasurer).

Companion to 02-demo-spine-architecture.html §4 (Move 0 lifecycle), 04-artifact-contracts.html (per-artifact specs), 09-business-case-pattern-setter.html (the Phase 4 output mobilization consumes). Reuses CSS from 02 (paper · ink · accent · serif Georgia · sans DM Sans).

Section 1 · What a mobilization plan is — and isn't

What it is

A live delivery contract. Every milestone has a named owner, a measurable evidence-of-completion, an explicit prerequisite chain, and a real-time status. It ships when the prior phase's artifacts (strategy memo + architecture + business case) are approved. It is consumed weekly by the workstream owners and monthly by the L0 sponsor and the audit committee.

What it isn't

A Gantt chart with pretty bars and aspirational "complete training" milestones. A static MS Project file emailed quarterly. A self-reported RAG status with no evidence. A "we'll figure out who owns Cap 3 later" plan. Sentinel will not generate this plan unless every milestone has an owner and an evidence-of-completion that resolves to something measurable in substrate.

Operational rule 1 — Foundation before AI

From the package's five locked rules. No AI use case milestone can be not-blocked until its foundation milestone is shipped. The plan UI enforces this: AI capability cards display the foundation milestone they're blocked on; you cannot mark them in-flight without an override that threads to the substrate as an audit event.

Operational rule 2 — No fake completion

A milestone ticks to "shipped" only when its evidence-of-completion criterion resolves true against substrate. "All 48 Kyriba users have logged in ≥ 3 times in past 14 days" resolves against the loaded auth log. "Variance < 0.05%" resolves against the ERP feed reconciliation table. Aspirational checkboxes are rejected at draft time.

How to read this graph

Section 7 · Owner assignment workflow

Sentinel pre-drafts owners from prior phase outputs. Aisha can reassign with rationale; reassignment threads to substrate as an audit event. No milestone can ship without a named owner; "TBD" is rejected.

1
Sentinel drafts owner from prior phase artifact

Example: "Move 0 G1 owner = Group Treasurer (A. Vargas), per architecture artifact arch.kyriba-banking-connectivity.md §Owners. Procurement Lead = R for RFP execution per business case §Investment Plan."

2
Aisha reviews + accepts or reassigns with rationale

Reassign click opens "name + rationale" mini-form. Rationale is required (Sentinel rejects empty). Reassignment writes owner_change event with before/after, rationale, timestamp, actor.

3
Owner gets named + notified through their primary channel

Substrate-side: writes to milestone_owner (current) and milestone_owner_history (audit). UI-side: notification to the named owner; their personal "things I own this week" rail picks it up.

4
Sentinel validates RACI completeness before plan accept

Plan cannot move from Draft → Accepted while any milestone has no Accountable or any workstream has no Consulted on a PortCo-touching gate. Acceptance is the one-click action that triggers the page going live + Sentinel beginning its weekly trajectory checks.

5
Owner change mid-flight

Any time after Accepted. Same rationale-required UX. Posts to substrate as an audit event with reason_code (departure · reassignment · escalation · scope-shift). L0 sponsor sees ownership-change rate in Tower as a soft signal.

Section 8 · Live status · how milestones tick

Milestones tick to "shipped" automatically when their EoC resolves true against substrate. Aisha doesn't update RAG status — she watches it.

What "shipped" means

The substrate query, checksum, or attestation defined by the EoC resolves true. For example, G1-M1 ticks to shipped when the banking_inventory table has 14 rows for Morgan Street tenant with required columns non-null AND the variance check vs GL bank ledger is zero. The transition writes milestone_shipped_at. No self-report.

What "blocked" means

An in-flight or not-started milestone has at least one prereq that is not yet shipped past its declared transition deadline. Computed each refresh cycle. Surfaces in red. Sentinel's "what's blocking X" chat answer pulls from this same computed state — one source of truth.

What "at-risk" means

Trajectory-based. Sentinel projects to the due date using current rate (e.g., login-rate growth for adoption) and flags if projected ship-date > due-date by > 5 working days. Forecast must cite the substrate signal — no vibes-based "at risk" calls.

How blockers surface

EoC fails → milestone stays in flight past due → block ripples downstream (any milestone with this as a prereq surfaces blocked-by) → Sentinel's daily summary names them in priority order → owner gets a notification → blocker incident lands on the L0 Tower under "concentration risk · execution".

Section 9 · The 30/60/90 cadence rule

Why 30/60/90 and not a different window? Three reasons. (1) PE-style cadence: portfolio companies and operating partners are wired to think in 90-day execution sprints anchored to board cycles. (2) Forecast decay: detail beyond 90 days is mostly guesswork; rather than fake it, defer it. (3) Re-plan cycle: every 30 days the plan is re-baselined as one column ticks off and a new one is drafted in.

Day 1–30 · dominant column

Most milestone cards. Daily-resolution detail. Owners assigned with no slack. EoC criteria fully specified. This is where the work happens this month — the page reader's primary focus.

Day 31–60 · secondary

Mid-detail. Owners assigned. EoC drafted. Acknowledged that some of these will re-baseline based on day 1–30 learnings. Sentinel will refresh the milestones on day 30 with the actual day-1–30 outcomes.

Day 61–90 · tertiary

Headline milestones only. Owner-named but slim on detail. Functions as the "what does done look like" anchor. Detail-resolution comes when the day-60 refresh promotes it into the 30-day column.

Beyond day 90 — deferred to next mobilization refresh

If the Move spans > 90 days (Move 2 vendor consolidation is the obvious case — typical RFP-to-cutover is 120–180 days), Phase 5 emits a "90+ tail" companion artifact that flags the headline gates after day 90. Detailed planning for that tail is a fresh mobilization cycle, drafted on day 75 of the current cycle so it lands accepted before day 90.

Section 11 · Phase exit · readiness scorecard

The bottom of the page. Every Phase 5 ends with a single, computed, evidence-backed scorecard that answers: are we ready to enter the next phase / next Move? For Move 0 → Move 1, the rule per the demo spine is "Move 0 G1–G4 minimum green" (from 02-demo-spine-architecture.html §12).

Gate Readiness criterion Evidence Status
G1 Banking connectivity wave 1 complete · 4 strategic banks H2H-live · zero P1 incidents in 7-day window G1-M1 · G1-M4 shipped + bank_h2h_incidents table Track
G2 ERP feed daily variance < 0.05% sustained over rolling 30-day window G2-M2 shipped + feed_recon table 30-day query Track
G3 Entity registry + IC matrix complete · all PortCos · zero unresolved IC pairs G3-M1 + G3-M2 shipped + entity_ic_matrix unresolved-count = 0 Track
G4 Silver layer normalized · 18+ months continuous clean data available for model training G4-M1 + G4-M2 shipped + silver_position_eccd row-count + checksum Risk
G5 90% weekly-active sustained 60 days · acknowledged as soft for Move 1 entry G5-M2 shipped + auth log 60-day query Pending
G6 IC auto-recon delivers T+1 month-end close · not required for Move 1 entry but unlocks Cap 4 G6-M3 shipped + close_cycle_days table Pending
Move 1 entry condition (canonical)

Move 1 mobilization auto-drafts only when G1, G2, G3, G4 all show green in this scorecard. G5/G6 are not blockers (G5 is adoption, can run in parallel · G6 is an AI capability itself). This is the foundation-before-AI rule made operational for the Move 0 → Move 1 transition. Sentinel will not let Move 1 Phase 5 begin drafting until these four go green; attempting to start it returns a substrate-level "phase entry condition not met" error with the failing gate named.

Section 12 · How this template flexes per Move

Same skeleton (page header · 30/60/90 swimlane · RACI · dependency graph · chat rail · readiness scorecard). The shape of the milestones and the ratio of foundation-to-AI varies. This section sketches each Move's flex.

Move 0 · Kyriba De-Risk (this page)
Per HoldCo · 90 days · 6 gates × ~3 milestones each + governance
Foundation 30d
Connectivity 60d
Cutover 90d

~17 milestones. Foundation dominates day 1–30 (5 of 9). Adoption sprint anchors day 31–60 (G5-M2 + GOV-M1). Cutover + first month-end with auto-IC anchor day 61–90.

Move 1 · AI on top of Kyriba
Per HoldCo · 90 days · 4 AI caps with foundation-first sequencing
Lakehouse + Unity 30d
Cap 1 + Cap 4 30–60
Cap 2 + Cap 3 60–90

Day 1–30 is all foundation — Databricks lakehouse target, Unity Catalog for financial data, model registry, HIL gate config. Every Cap 1–4 card has blocked_until: foundation_milestone_X. Caps 1 + 4 (data dependency lower) go 30–60; Caps 2 + 3 (covenant + BEC fraud) go 60–90 because they need 2 months of clean Silver-layer data.

Move 2 · Vendor Consolidation
L0 federated · 90+ days · extends beyond window
Discovery 30d
Slate + spawns 60d
Negotiation 90d
Transition 120d+

90-day window covers discovery + slate finalization + Source spawns + initial negotiation. The "90+ tail" companion artifact carries vendor-by-vendor transition into days 91–180. Refresh cadence flips to quarterly with per-category PortCo CFO socialization.

Move 3 · Federated IT Strategy
L0 cross-HoldCo · 90 days · sets standing operating cadence
Operating review setup 30d
Marketplace catalog 30–60
Wave coordinator standup 60–90

Day 1–30 stands up the L0 OP-Tech federated operating review (charter, cadence, agenda template). Day 31–60 publishes Lakefront's AI capability marketplace + cloud landing-zone standards. Day 61–90 names the Workday/Snowflake wave coordinator + first wave standup. After day 90 the operating review runs steady-state.

Move 4 · Federated Risk + Governance
L0 continuous · ad-hoc spawns when concentration thresholds cross
Baseline + threshold setup 30–60d
Continuous + ad-hoc spawns

Initial 30-day window establishes concentration risk thresholds + signs them off with L0 CCO. After day 30 Move 4 runs continuous; mobilization cards are spawned ad-hoc when a threshold is crossed (e.g., "cyber carrier concentration > 67% triggers Move 4 ad-hoc event · spawns its own 30/60/90 mini-plan").

Move 0 · Kyriba multi-HoldCo (when Roosevelt rolls out)
Federated playbook reuse · timeline compresses 40%
Foundation 18d
Connectivity 36d
Cutover 54d
Buffer

When Roosevelt picks up Kyriba using Morgan Street + Lakefront's shared playbook, the same 17-milestone skeleton compresses 40% (per Gartner platform-rollout standardization patterns). The dependency graph is identical; the EoC criteria are reused; ownership changes (Roosevelt's open Treasurer role gets filled). Sentinel pre-drafts from the prior HoldCo's accepted plan as the seed.

Section 14 · Audit + telemetry posture

What gets written to the substrate audit log
  • Plan drafted by Sentinel (with input artifact IDs)
  • Plan accepted by named owner
  • Each milestone ship transition (auto from EoC) with substrate query that resolved true
  • Each blocker incident (which prereq failed, when, downstream impact)
  • Each owner change with before/after, rationale, actor
  • Each RACI change post-acceptance
  • Each phase exit signoff with full readiness scorecard snapshot
What telemetry surfaces in Tower (L0 view)
  • Per-Move per-HoldCo plan health (shipped / in flight / blocked counts)
  • Cross-HoldCo blocker concentration (e.g., "all 3 HoldCos blocked on ERP feed quality this month — federated SI consideration")
  • Owner-change rate as a soft execution-risk signal
  • Plan acceptance latency (draft → accepted)
  • EoC failure rate (blockers that never resolve in window) as a planning-quality signal — high rate means EoCs were drawn too aggressively at draft time

Section 16 · Anti-patterns this page rejects

Aspirational milestones

"Complete training." "Improve adoption." "Drive quality." Rejected at draft. Sentinel returns: "this milestone has no measurable EoC — translate to a substrate query, a checksum, or a named-artifact attestation."

TBD ownership

"Owner: TBD." "We'll figure out later who owns this." Rejected at draft. Sentinel returns: "name an Accountable or this milestone cannot be in the accepted plan."

Self-reported RAG

"Treasury thinks G5 is green." Status is not aspirational — it's substrate-evaluated. The owner cannot manually flip a milestone to "shipped"; only the EoC evaluator can.

AI before foundation

"Let's pilot Cap 3 in parallel with the lakehouse build." Rejected at the dependency graph. The Cap 3 card stays blocked until the foundation milestones it depends on ship. Override requires a substrate-logged exception with named approver.

The 6-month Gantt

"Plan goes out 6 months." Rejected at the 90-day window. Beyond 90 is the "90+ tail" companion artifact (Move 2 typical case) — headline milestones only, with the expectation of a fresh mobilization cycle drafted on day 75.

Single-owner Accountable + Responsible

"Same person owns and does it." Allowed but flagged. Sentinel notes "single point of execution risk" in the page header. The plan ships; the risk is visible to L0.

Section 17 · Quality bar · the four tests Aisha runs

Test What Aisha can do in < 10 seconds Why it matters
1 See what's happening this week, next month, next quarter at a glance. 30/60/90 columns + scorecard row carry the whole story. No drill-down required for the at-a-glance.
2 Know exactly who owns what without asking. Owner chip on every milestone + RACI matrix beneath. No "let me check" lookup.
3 Identify blockers in 5 seconds. Red left-border, scorecard count, dependency graph with dashed nodes, Sentinel chat one prompt away.
4 Trust the plan because every milestone has a measurable "done" definition. EoC line on every card. Status is evaluated from substrate, not self-reported. No fake completion possible.
